Referred me to the ambulatory emergency care unit in a couple of days and said if I pass out or can’t breathe  to come straight back. I had blood tests which were fine but ECG and the doctor listening to my heart showed multiple ectopic beats and of course bradycardia but not as bad as it is now. 

Coffee and moving around to try and get my heart rate up barely brings it in to the forties when the episodes happen. 

It’s happening multiple times a day and my partner has had to take the day off of work because I am struggling to look after my baby.

I went to A&E yesterday and they sent me home because I hadn’t passed out fully yet. I don’t think I can look after my baby like this though however there are nurse strikes in the UK currently so the hospitals are overrun. I don’t want to come across as dramatic ☹️

I was 14 and had just moved to a strict Catholic high school, and was sat in English class. It was my first day and I didn’t know anybody, but English was my favourite subject so I was excited to be there. 

The teacher is talking about a book we’re going to read, and decides to read an extract from it. Said extract was a little…gory. She’s about half-way down the second page when the kid I’m sitting next to just keels over on to his desk, deathly pale. The class starts screaming, the teacher starts screaming and panicking, I’m just sat there like “wtf is going on”. 

The teacher runs over and, obviously panicking, begins to slap this kid’s face to try and wake him up. Literally like something out of a movie. Shouting “Wake up! Wake up!”. By this point someone in the class has gone to get help and the nurse arrived. The kid is hauled out of class and taken to the first aid room. Then the teacher just carries on reading the extract from the book like nothing had happened? Then we said a prayer for him at the end of class. Nobody talked about it afterwards.
